name: Giving What We Can (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Moves money: each recipient its donors give to, read live, brings its own countries.
summary: Giving What We Can promotes effective giving through the 10% Pledge, research on where to give and a donation platform; this model covers all its spending in 2023 and 2024 ($3.9M in 2024 prices, run by Effective Ventures until August 2024 and by its own UK and US charities after). At the defaults it averts about 56 years of healthy life per $1,000: its 1,347 new 10% Pledges, 1,259 Trial Pledges and other donors' platform giving add up to about $34M it caused (by its donor surveys a third of pledgers' giving and 28% of others' would not have happened without it), each dollar valued at the charities its donors actually gave to, each at its figure on the rankings (mostly GiveWell's top charities), half of it counted as new money, the next dollar at 42% of the past average. It moves about nine dollars, most of it to top global-health charities, for each dollar it spends. The result moves most with the discount rate (pledgers give for 35 years), its next-dollar figure, the value of a life and where shifted money would otherwise have gone; no branch is discounted for missing data, since money moved is counted.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Discounted years of giving per new pledge (share still giving each year, summed)
rows.explainer: The shared pledge-persistence figures (facts/meta.json, from Giving What We Can's cohort data): the share of pledgers giving in year t is floor + (first year − floor) × (1 − decay)^t, each year discounted at the site's rate. The fading part is an annuity at the combined rate (1 + discount) / (1 − decay) − 1. About 6.3 at 4%.

Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium, Helen Keller Intl, New Incentives), each at GiveWell's figure for the charity on the rankings (its programmes and locations weighted by funding) under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to the charities Giving What We Can's donors gave to (its 2023–2024 split, live), units of value
rows.explainer: Where its donors' money went in 2023–2024 (its donation classification sheet), each recipient at its figure on the rankings under your values (the charity's, its programmes and locations weighted by funding), by the site's rule for a split (normalization.md 2.8). Of the giving, 82% (55–90%) went to recipients it rates high-impact; the rest, to charities it couldn't place, is valued as an ordinary charity (the shared prior multiple of GiveDirectly). The high-impact part by cause, its weights: global health and wellbeing ($40.2M): GiveWell-following funds at GiveWell's Top Charities (value_global_health), and the named charities with a model here (Against Malaria Foundation, GiveDirectly, Malaria Consortium, Helen Keller Intl, New Incentives, Deworm the World at Evidence Action's figure, Unlimit Health, StrongMinds), weighted by their money; the smaller recipients take that average; animal welfare ($9.8M): The Humane League (ACE's figure, the one the rankings show), the only animal recipient it names that the site models (the Animal Welfare Fund, ACE's and its own animal funds take its figure); catastrophic risk ($11.5M): none of its recipients (Long-Term Future Fund, Longview, its Risks and Resilience Fund) has a model, so the catastrophic-risk charities on the rankings, equal weights (#cause:catastrophic-risk). Climate change ($6.3M: no published model of the climate work its donors fund) and movement building ($10.9M: other meta charities) take the average of the rest.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: 1× GiveDirectly), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Shifted money was going to be given anyway; it is credited only for the gain. Where it would have gone is valued at GiveDirectly's live result (GiveWell's model), as Ambitious Impact does, times a shared multiple (1×, from 0 to 3×).

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: Side effects of the money moved, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: Good and harm beyond the donations counted: pledgers who bring friends and colleagues to give without signing up through it, and its public research used by donors who never visit (positive); a 10% norm that anchors some who would have given more, and donor attention drawn from other good uses (negative). The shared figure for these effects (facts/meta.json): 5% (−5% to +20%) of the modelled value; its evaluation leaves these out ('it doesn't model all of our impact').

rows.label: Value of the money moved (units of value)
rows.explainer: Money moved × the net value of a dollar moved, with the side effects.
